blocks.text: Things marked in Yellow mean that I am not sold, and that I am not sold that the players are sold. That being said, I am issuing this as a Hotfix to give those changes the best chance I can (because I do believe in them.) If they are truly non-starters, or if when put on the table these changes are not working in a way that’s meaningfully better (vibes or gameplay wise) I will 100% go in a different direction. I am not a monster here, but I do have strong opinions and a keyboard. This is also why there are many more interesting changes I’ve seen suggested that are not included below. This is more of a .1 take two. And if the design philosophy changes significantly for .2 I’ll need to factor in everything else as well. The goal here is to get this thing as close to a satisfying document as possible for as many players as possible. That’s not just me, the fanboys or the detractors, that’s everyone…. blocks.text: I understand that Daemons do not run away or panic in the traditional sense. However they are described in the lore as being fickle and tenuously attached to the mortal world. They are dynamic and magical. While it may make sense that a Plaguebearer of Nurgle or a Bloodletter of Khorne would stand there to receive a charge regardless of the consequences - this simply does not translate to Slaanesh or to Tzeentch. We are talking about creatures that can move like lightning, or, see the future. Furthermore, although Daemons are not afraid of death in the mortal sense - being ripped from reality and banished back to the Realm of Chaos for an indefinite time out isn’t exactly their main goal of swinging through the mortal realms. Secondly - although Immune to Psychology since 6th edition, Daemons have also had Daemonic Instability. This is the mechanic that serves as the representation of the Daemon’s loose grasp on reality. It is similar, but different, to unstable - and requires players to understand another alternative way to resolve a break test. But thematically and mechanically Daemonic Instability is the Daemon version of a leadership check. So why not use it more when appropriate?
